title: Quarterly Roadmap Simulation: Hosted Endpoint Capacity & Model Catalog Contingency Grid
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a cross-functional quarterly planning simulation that ties hosted endpoint capacity lanes to model catalog commitments and OKR risk tiers. Goal: produce a contingency grid and decision playbook that PMs and Eng can use when model rotations, unexpected model regressions, or capacity constraints threaten SLA/expense targets. Deliverables: contingency grid (matrix of failure modes x actions), a canary/fallback policy proposal, and a condensed runbook for on-call and solutions architects.
acceptance_criteria: Contingency grid (CSV + one-page summary) that maps 6 failure modes to 3 prioritized actions
A canary + fallback policy draft approved by Runtime and Infra leads
Cost/latency impact model for each contingency lane with example numbers
One-page runbook shared in #pm-roadmap and included in Sprint Kickoff deck
updates: 2026-01-14: Kickoff meeting with Runtime (Lina), Infra (Marcus), DX (Rina). Agreed scope: focus on hosted endpoints used by top 10 customers by spend + Tiered model catalog (stable, beta, experimental). Action: PM to synthesize historical incidents for 18 months.

2026-01-21: Pulled incident runbook and spike data from Incidents dashboard. Noted two recurring capacity saturation windows tied to batch-size regression in runtime-1.18. Assigned ENG follow-up (ENG-4019) to quantify KV cache hit-rate impact on token latency.

2026-02-02: Drafted contingency grid v0.1. Trade-offs discussion in review: aggressive fallback to quantized model reduces latency but may raise hallucination risk; noted need for A/B quality checks (RINA to own evaluation harness).
2026-02-10: PM review with Solutions Engineering. Feedback: add customer-facing communication templates and escalate matrix. Added 'customer_impact' metric per lane. Diego to draft comms.

2026-02-22: Runtime team proposed an automated routing policy prototype (route-by-cost fallback) for two lanes; flagged storage of KV caches as a potential blocker for private deployments. Open question for Platform: add alignment ticket for Private (PM follow-up).
2026-03-01: Economics model completed for three contingency lanes (numbers in linked sheet). Preliminary approval from Finance for conservative cost delta assumptions (+8% worst-case monthly).

2026-03-05: Shared canary/fallback policy draft in RFC-threads. Awaiting Eng Architecture signoff and legal review of customer comms. Next: finalize one-page runbook and embed triggers into Console alerts (ENG-3321 dependency).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Prefer rollback-to-stable-model vs on-the-fly quantized fallback: rollback has better quality guarantees but higher latency to execute for large fleets (decision: hybrid - immediate route-by-cost fallback for low-risk routes; staged rollback for high-risk customers).
Automated routing increases complexity in Private deployments; decision: include gated toggle and require explicit approval for customer-managed clusters.
Canary window sizing tradeoff: wider windows detect regressions earlier but increase exposure; default to 5% traffic for 24h with fast rollback triggers.
risks: Model quality regressions from quantized fallbacks (mitigation: prompt-level evals and rollback thresholds)
Insufficient observability for multi-tenant capacity spikes (mitigation: add token-level heatmaps and per-route SLO alerts)
Operational burden on on-call during multi-customer incidents (mitigation: create runbook and pre-approved comms templates)
Private deployment KV cache constraints preventing fast fallbacks (mitigation: documented limitations and customer-specific runbooks)
Potential +8% monthly cost in worst-case contingency activation (Finance approved conservative buffer)
